collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A child asks why couples hop at every wedding: tell the official reason, or ask what the child thinks.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At every wedding on Isola, the couple takes three steps forward, then a little hop, then three steps more. It's a lovely, solemn moment. (friend) has just asked (subject) why there's a hop. (subject) has always been told it means the couple will leap over any troubles together.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells (friend) about leaping over troubles. (friend) is satisfied. Then (elder), an elder sitting nearby, snorts. "That's not why," (elder) says. "Long ago, at somebody's wedding, a crab ran across the path, and the bride jumped over it, and everyone thought it was so lucky they've done it ever since." (subject) stares. (friend) is delighted. Both reasons are told from then on.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) has a theory: somebody tripped. Or the ground was hot. Or they were really, really happy and couldn't help it. (subject) laughs and says those are all good reasons. At the next wedding, the couple do the hop, and (friend) watches very closely to see which reason it looks like. (friend.He/she) decides it's the happy one.
